title: The North Face Minibus 23 review: steep walls from reverse-combi poles
dek: A freestanding two-person, three-season tent with four DAC Featherlite poles, two doors and two vestibules. Here's how its pole layout buys headroom.

body:
## The short version

The Minibus 23 is a freestanding two-person, three-season tent with two doors and two vestibules. Its standout design choice is the poles: a reverse-combi layout with thicker poles across the top and thinner poles down the sides, which pulls the walls steeper and adds headroom. There are few owner reviews online, so this guide is built from the published design and specs.

## Space

The floor is 84 by 50 inches, about 33 square feet, with a 39.5-inch interior height. That fits two standard pads side by side, and the steep walls keep the fabric off your face. The two vestibules total about 20 square feet, enough to keep packs and wet boots out of the sleeping area.

## Materials and weather

The fly is PU-coated ripstop nylon with DWR, and the bathtub floor is 70-denier nylon taffeta with a 5,000 mm coating and fully taped seams. Those are solid three-season numbers. On any used Minibus, check the fly coating and seam tape: older North Face flies from this era can turn sticky or peel.

## Setup

It's freestanding with clips, so it pitches quickly and can be moved after it's up. It also supports a fast pitch using the fly, poles and footprint without the inner tent.

## Poles and parts

The Minibus 23 uses **4 poles**, **DAC Featherlite**.

Because the set mixes thicker roof poles with thinner side poles, a replacement has to match both diameter and position. Keep the set together when you pack it.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Minibus 23 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Minibus%2023), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

The Minibus 23 is a well-designed two-door tent for two backpackers. Buy used on condition, and keep the four poles together as a matched set, since the top and side poles differ.
